messages:
Anya P.: Hi team — got a ticket from an employee. Specialist visit was billed with the wrong CPT, insurer marked it out-of-network and denied. EOB shows CPT 99203 but provider billed 99050 (??). Need next steps to get this fixed and a timeline for the employee.
Marcus C.: Ugh. First step: ask provider to issue a corrected claim with the right CPT. We'll also file an appeal with the insurer in parallel.
Anya P.: Thanks — employee wants a short checklist I can send them. Can you drop a template?
Marcus C.: Yep. Use this for the insurer appeal email:```Subject: Appeal - Claim denied for [MemberName] DOB [MM/DD/YYYY] - Claim #[claim_number]Attachments: 1) EOB 2) Itemized bill 3) Corrected claim (if available)Body: Please review the attached documents. The claim was denied due to an incorrect CPT on the provider submission. We request a reprocessing with CPT 99203. Contact: benefits@redwood.com```
Samira O.: Also ask the employee to request an itemized bill and the billing office's contact. If provider submits corrected claim it usually moves faster. I can open a broker escalation if they push back.
Anya P.: What about emergency or urgent care rules? This was a same-day specialist consult after ER discharge. Insurer marked it OON citing prior-authorization missing.
Marcus C.: For services tied to an ER visit there's often an emergency/associated-care exception. Submit appeal + ER discharge summary + clinical notes. Add: "Associated care to ER visit" in the appeal body. If insurer cites auth, include clinical justification.
benefits-bot: Automated: Typical appeal timelines are 30 calendar days for standard appeals, 72 hours for urgent (if clinical info supports). See: https://insurer.example/appeals-guide
Priya S.: I can send a short provider billing template to the practice billing team — often they just need the right CPT + tax ID to rebill. Here's a brief you can paste:```Hello billing team, Please re-submit claim for patient [Name], DOS [MM/DD/YYYY] under CPT 99203. Previous submission used 99050 which caused an OON denial. Attached: member EOB and itemized bill. Please confirm when corrected claim submitted and provide resubmission confirmation number. Thank you. - People Ops```
Anya P.: Adding employee details now: last 4 is 4321, member ID ends with X987, provider is Maple Specialty Clinic. I sent the billing template to their billing@maplespecialty.com.
Samira O.: Great — I'll open a broker case as backup. Can you forward me the EOB and itemized bill when you have them?
Anya P.: Forwarded. Also asked the provider to mark the claim as "Corrected Claim" and include the original claim number.
Marcus C.: If provider reprocesses, insurer re-adjudicates and member should see adjustment. If insurer refuses, we'll escalate with state consumer protections and surprise billing rules.
Priya S.: Note for the employee: if you need proof of coverage while this is pending, use the digital ID card in the benefits portal and save the confirmation email from us.
Anya P.: Thanks all. I'll update thread when provider confirms. :thumbsup:
Marcus C.: Thanks. Expect 30-45 days for a standard appeal, might be faster if corrected claim submitted within 7-10 business days.
Samira O.: Marking this as tracked in our benefits case tracker (case #BP-2026-201).
Anya P.: Provider just replied — they resubmitted with CPT 99203 and gave resub ID 555-178. Forwarding confirmation to employee now. :tada:
